text:
Hullo colleagues,
The cargo liaison asked me to write about shade areas, and I need everyone to treat this as a real safety note, not a casual reminder. When carriers are left in bright staging spots, the animals inside can overheat fast, and even brief exposure can turn into a welfare issue before the handoff is complete. Please keep crate checks calm, keep the path to loading clear, and move any animal out of direct sun as soon as a safe shaded spot is open.

We also need cleaner handoffs with the senior coordinator when a case starts to look messy. If a traveler reports a missing crate, use the normal review path and keep your language plain, respectful, and brief. <<FACT F118>> Do not make promises you cannot back up, and do not leave the traveler waiting with no update while the team sorts out the next step. If a crate is sitting where heat, glare, or wind could cause stress, tell the lead right away and keep watching it until it is moved. Louie, if mentioned in a file, should get the same patient handling and calm voice as any other pet, because the animal does not know why the delay is happening.

I am asking everyone at Aurelia Skyways in the Companion Animal Travel Desk to stay sharp on these small details, since the small details are what keep a routine move from turning into a welfare complaint. Use direct, respectful communication, and escalate early if the situation looks off. We can always slow the process for a moment, but we cannot undo a bad handoff after the fact. Please take this seriously and act on it right away.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
